summary: The 12 FIXED full-slide templates the deck2 viewer renders (SlideView switch in deck2/archetypes.tsx). An archetype is a whole-slide layout with a fixed slot geometry and one recognizable rhetorical shape (a hero, a binary choice, a decision matrix, an ask/CTA, ...). Contrast: a component-based layout is a FREE composition of kit components solved per-slide. Pick an archetype when the content IS one of these known patterns; compose freely when it is not.
selection_guide:
Pick an archetype in three ordered checks, then fall back to free composition if none clears them.

1. SHAPE — take the slide's dominant claim shape and read its best-fit archetype off SHAPE_AFFINITY (compiler/archetypes.py): metric->card-set/framework-tiles/hero; delta->framework-tiles/classification-table/binary-choice; comparison->decision-matrix/binary-choice/classification-table/framework-tiles; sequence->flow-sequence/scenario-beats; relationship->ask-cta/flow-sequence/scenario-beats; proportion->proportion-bars/framework-tiles; quote->disclosure-list/hero; set->card-set/disclosure-list/lens-reframe; trend->proportion-bars/flow-sequence; narrative->hero/disclosure-list/binary-choice; verdict->classification-table/ask-cta/disclosure-list. A data-bearing archetype only FAITHFULLY renders the shapes in its `carries` (ARCHETYPE_SHAPES) — a mismatched shape draws empty bars / overflowing cards. hero, ask-cta, disclosure-list and lens-reframe are shape-AGNOSTIC and safe for any dominant shape (the feasibility fallback).

2. CARDINALITY — the dominant claim's collection size must fit the archetype's primary-slot band (PRIMARY_ARRAY_SLOT + capacity). A 6-option comparison will NOT fit binary-choice (exactly 2) or decision-matrix (max 5); a 3-item roadmap will NOT fit flow-sequence (min 4). Outside the band -> different archetype or free composition.

3. DEPTH/DENSITY — respect the level band (LEVEL_POOL): L0 overview = sparse cover only (hero, ask-cta); L1 structured = density_rank >= 2; L2 detail = density_rank >= 3. Density must not DECREASE as depth increases (vertical monotonicity), and two dense archetypes must not sit adjacent at L1 (dense-adjacent-dense ban).

If all three clear -> use the archetype (fixed, pixel-faithful, instantly legible). If the shape is heterogeneous, the cardinality overflows every band, or the slide needs a bespoke arrangement of mixed parts -> drop to a free component composition (see archetype_vs_component_guide).

entries.name: Hero
entries.one_liner: The deck/topic opener — big title, lede, and optional persona + meta strip.
entries.carries: The cover statement. Shape-agnostic; built for a narrative/quote scalar claim that sets up the whole deck or topic. No data collection — it frames, it does not itemize.
when_to_use: Slide 1 of a deck, or the L0 overview cell of a topic
You need a strong title + one-line lede and nothing dense yet
You want to introduce the audiences (persona pills) or key facts (meta strip) up front
avoid_when: The slide has real itemized data to show (list, table, steps, bars) — a hero has no body slot for it
You are past the opening and need density (hero is sparse cover, L0 only)
entries.capacity: personas <= 4, meta <= 5. No primary data collection.
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx Hero(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['hero'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['hero']; kit board/archetypes/01-hero.html

entries.name: Lens Reframe
entries.one_liner: The same content seen through 2-4 switchable audience lenses (interactive tabs).
entries.carries: One set of points re-told per audience. Shape-agnostic; built for a `set` claim where the SAME material must be reframed for different personas (each tab = one persona, each pane = that persona's bullet rows).
when_to_use: The message changes by audience and you want the reader to toggle perspectives
You have 2-4 personas, each with up to ~7 disclosure rows
Multi-stakeholder decks where 'what this means for YOU' is the point
avoid_when: There is only one audience / one framing (use disclosure-list)
The content differs in KIND per tab rather than in framing — that is separate slides
A static export where interactivity is lost (only the active pane shows)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx LensReframe(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['lens-reframe'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['lens-reframe']; kit board/archetypes/02-lens-reframe.html

entries.name: Disclosure List
entries.one_liner: A ranked list of 3-7 points, each optionally expandable to a detail body.
entries.carries: A progressive list. Shape-agnostic default carrier — narrative/quote/set/verdict all downcast here safely. Each row = a titled point with optional sub, and an expand-on-click detail. The universal fallback when no data-viz archetype fits.
when_to_use: 3-7 discrete points that share no common metric/axis
You want headline-first reading with detail on demand (click to expand)
The safe choice when the claim shape has no dedicated visualization
avoid_when: Items compare on the same criteria (use decision-matrix / classification-table)
Items are ordered steps (use flow-sequence) or magnitudes (use proportion-bars)
Fewer than 3 points — too thin for a full slide
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx DisclosureList()/BulletList(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['disclosure-list'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['disclosure-list']; kit board/archetypes/03-disclosure-list.html

entries.name: Scenario Beats
entries.one_liner: A chronological walkthrough — 3-10 time/marker-stamped beats + optional callout.
entries.carries: A narrated sequence or story. Built for `sequence` (and `quote`) claims: each beat is a moment (mark + body + optional who), read top-to-bottom as a timeline of events, with a summary callout.
when_to_use: A story, day-in-the-life, or event timeline told as beats
You want prose-y moments (who did what) rather than a rigid tool/step chain
3-10 beats plus a closing takeaway callout
avoid_when: The sequence is a mechanical process with actors/tools/timing (use flow-sequence)
Items are not ordered in time (use disclosure-list / card-set)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx ScenarioBeats(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['scenario-beats'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['scenario-beats']; kit board/archetypes/04-scenario-beats.html

entries.name: Decision Matrix
entries.one_liner: 3-5 competing options compared on the same criteria, one marked recommended.
entries.carries: A `comparison` claim with 3-5 options. Each option is a card of key/value criteria lines; the recommended one is highlighted. The canonical 'which option do we pick' slide.
when_to_use: 3-5 alternatives evaluated on shared criteria (cost, risk, effort...)
You want to steer to a recommendation while showing the trade-offs
Vendor / architecture / approach selection
avoid_when: Exactly 2 options — use binary-choice (cleaner this-vs-that)
More than 5 options — overflows; use classification-table
Options do NOT share criteria (use card-set)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx DecisionMatrix(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['decision-matrix'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['decision-matrix']; kit board/archetypes/05-decision-matrix.html

entries.name: Framework Tiles
entries.one_liner: 3-5 KPI/definition tiles (value + label + desc) plus an optional support table.
entries.carries: `metric`/`proportion`/`delta`/`comparison` claims as headline tiles. Each tile foregrounds a big value with a label; an optional table carries the backing detail. The 'here are the numbers/pillars' slide.
when_to_use: 3-5 headline metrics, pillars, or definitions to show at a glance
You want big values front-and-centre with an optional detail table below
Framework / model with named components
avoid_when: Values are parts of one whole / ranked magnitudes (use proportion-bars)
Items are ordered steps (use flow-sequence)
Only 2 things and they oppose each other (use binary-choice)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx FrameworkTiles(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['framework-tiles'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['framework-tiles']; kit board/archetypes/06-framework-tiles.html

entries.name: Binary Choice
entries.one_liner: Exactly two mutually-exclusive paths (this vs that) + a verdict callout.
entries.carries: A `comparison`/`delta` claim with EXACTLY 2 sides. Each path is a toned card (warn vs recommend/accent) with eyebrow, title, body, footer; the callout delivers the verdict. Built for the fork-in-the-road decision.
when_to_use: A true either/or: two options, one usually preferred
You want maximum contrast and a clear steer between them
Build vs buy, migrate vs stay, risk vs safe path
avoid_when: There are 3+ options (use decision-matrix or classification-table)
The two things are complementary, not exclusive (use card-set / framework-tiles)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx BinaryChoice(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['binary-choice'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['binary-choice']; kit board/archetypes/07-binary-choice.html

entries.name: Classification Table
entries.one_liner: A per-row verdict table with method/verdict badges + a summary stat callout.
entries.carries: A `verdict`/`comparison`/`set` claim as a scannable table. Rows carry a verdict class (essential/nogo/redesign/redundant), method and verdict columns render as coloured badges, and a summary callout tallies the counts. The 'audit / triage / go-no-go' slide.
when_to_use: Many rows each needing a labelled verdict or category (keep/kill, pass/fail)
An audit, triage, or classification with a headline tally
More options than a decision-matrix can hold, evaluated categorically
avoid_when: Only 2-5 options weighed on criteria (use binary-choice / decision-matrix)
No per-row verdict/category — it is just a list (use disclosure-list)
entries.capacity: open-ended table rows; summary callout with stat tally.
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx ClassificationTable(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['classification-table'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['classification-table']; kit board/archetypes/08-classification-table.html

entries.name: Flow Sequence
entries.one_liner: A 4-8 step ordered process, each step tagged with actor / tool / timing.
entries.carries: A `sequence` claim as a mechanical pipeline. Each step is auto-numbered and coloured by actor (user/edge/cloud/process) with optional tool + ms label. The 'how the system works, step by step' slide.
when_to_use: An ordered process / pipeline / request lifecycle of 4-8 steps
You want to show WHO does each step (actor) and with what tool/latency
Onboarding flows, request paths, data pipelines
avoid_when: Fewer than 4 steps or the order does not matter (use card-set / disclosure-list)
The narrative is story-like moments, not tooled steps (use scenario-beats)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx FlowSequence(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['flow-sequence'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['flow-sequence'] + ORDINAL_SLOTS; kit board/archetypes/09-flow-sequence.html

entries.name: Proportion Bars
entries.one_liner: 2-8 labelled magnitudes as horizontal bars (part-to-whole or ranking).
entries.carries: A `proportion`/`trend` claim. Each row is a stage label + a percent-width bar (state-coloured safe/caution/danger) + a value. Built to make relative size or a distribution instantly visible.
when_to_use: Parts of a whole, a ranking, or a distribution with real percentages
You want the reader to SEE relative magnitude, not read numbers
Budget split, latency breakdown, share-of-X
avoid_when: The values are not comparable magnitudes (use framework-tiles / card-set)
Fewer than 2 rows, or no parseable numbers (bars render empty)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx ProportionBars(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['proportion-bars'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['proportion-bars']; kit board/archetypes/10-proportion-bars.html

entries.name: Card Set
entries.one_liner: 3-5 peer items as a card grid, with an optional stat row above.
entries.carries: A `set`/`metric` claim of sibling items with no shared axis. Each card is an icon + name + desc; an optional stat row surfaces headline numbers. The 'here are the N things' grid when they don't compare or sequence.
when_to_use: 3-5 peer items (features, capabilities, team, products) shown side by side
Items are equals — no ranking, no shared criteria, no order
You want an optional headline stat row above the grid
avoid_when: Items compare on criteria (use decision-matrix) or are ordered (use flow-sequence)
Items are magnitudes of one whole (use proportion-bars)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx CardSet(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['card-set'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['card-set']; kit board/archetypes/11-card-set.html

entries.name: Ask / CTA
entries.one_liner: The closing ask — a titled ask list + optional architecture diagram.
entries.carries: A `relationship`/`verdict` claim as a call to action. The ask box lists what you want; the optional arch diagram shows the target state (label/value items, ok/broken). The closer of a deck.
when_to_use: The final slide: what you want the audience to do / decide / fund
A concrete ask list, optionally paired with a target-state diagram
Pitch close, decision request, next-steps
avoid_when: You are not closing / not asking for anything (use hero or a content archetype)
The content is dense data (ask-cta is sparse cover, L0)
entries.source_ref: deck2/archetypes.tsx AskCta(); compiler/archetypes.py SLOTS['ask-cta'] + FILL_SCHEMAS['ask-cta']; kit board/archetypes/12-ask-cta.html

archetype_vs_component_guide.principle: An ARCHETYPE is a fixed, whole-slide template with one baked-in rhetorical shape and a fixed slot geometry; a COMPONENT-BASED LAYOUT is a free composition of kit components solved per slide. Both render through the same kit CSS. The single question that decides between them: does this slide's content collapse cleanly to ONE known pattern, or is it a heterogeneous mix that needs a bespoke arrangement? A known pattern -> archetype (clarity, recognizability, pixel-faithful reliability, no solve). A mix -> free composition. In the pipeline this is literal: build_deck_doc composes real kit HTML per cell and the viewer PREFERS the composed fragment, falling back to the fixed archetype downcast (to_deckdoc._archetype_for) only when composition is absent or fails.
pick_fixed_archetype_when: The slide IS a recognizable pattern the audience decodes instantly: a hero opener, a binary choice, a decision matrix, a proportion breakdown, an ordered process, an ask/CTA.
There is ONE dominant claim shape and the items are HOMOGENEOUS — all peers with the same structure (all options share criteria, all steps are steps, all bars are magnitudes).
The collection size FITS an archetype's primary-slot band (2 for binary-choice, 3-5 for decision-matrix/tiles/cards, 4-8 for flow-sequence, 2-8 for bars).
You want the rhetorical FORCE of a named pattern — the layout itself carries the argument (this-vs-that tension, one-recommended-option, part-of-whole).
You want deterministic, pixel-faithful output with no layout solve (fixed templates never overflow or need measuring).
The depth/density band wants a canonical cover: L0 overview -> hero or ask-cta.
pick_component_composition_when: The slide is HETEROGENEOUS — it mixes claim shapes: a stat AND a bullet list AND a quote, or a chart beside a callout beside a table. No single archetype's slot geometry holds all of it.
Cardinality OVERFLOWS every archetype band: 6+ comparison options, a 3-phase roadmap (below flow-sequence's min 4), 10+ classified rows past a table's comfortable read.
The content needs a BESPOKE arrangement — a specific spatial relationship (side-by-side chart+prose, nested groupings, an annotated diagram) no fixed template exposes.

The dominant shape has NO faithful archetype carrier for this content, so a downcast would render empty/overflowing junk (a non-proportion claim in proportion-bars = empty bars; a 6-option comparison crammed into binary-choice).
The material is genuinely one-off — not a repeatable pattern — and forcing it into a template would distort the meaning to fit the slots.
You need finer density control than the archetype's fixed load allows (e.g. a slide that must sit between two density bands).

archetype: Exactly two options that oppose -> binary-choice
3-5 options on shared criteria, one to recommend -> decision-matrix
Real percentages that sum toward a whole -> proportion-bars
A 4-8 step tooled pipeline with actors -> flow-sequence
3-5 equal peer items, no order/criteria -> card-set
Opening a deck / topic with a title + lede -> hero
Closing with a concrete request -> ask-cta
composition: 'A KPI, then three risks, then a quote' on one slide -> mixed shapes, compose
'Seven vendors across five criteria' -> overflows decision-matrix (max 5), compose a table+badges layout
'A diagram on the left, bullet commentary on the right' -> spatial pairing no archetype exposes, compose
'A 3-phase roadmap' -> below flow-sequence min (4), compose a 3-column layout
'A chart plus its own caption plus a warning callout' -> heterogeneous stack, compose

archetype_vs_component_guide.rule_of_thumb: If you can name the slide's pattern in two words (a binary choice, a decision matrix, a process flow, an ask) and the item count fits the band -> reach for the fixed ARCHETYPE for its clarity and reliability. The moment you find yourself saying 'and also...' about a DIFFERENT kind of content on the same slide, or the count won't fit -> drop the archetype and COMPOSE from components.
